3. The sample in the present was taken on 11.06.2019.

4. A perusal of the complaint in the present case reveals that in paragraph no.14, the complainant has, while making allegations against the accused, indicated the specific Regulations which seem to have been violated by accused by adding synthetic colour Tartrazine yellow to the food product.

The paragraph no.14 of the complaint is reproduced hereinbelow for ease of reference:

sentences.text: Part investigation was carried out by Sh. Bal Mukund, the then Food Safety Officer and then file was handed over to the undersigned on 21.10.19.

Ms. Kapil Malik conducted the further investigation investigation and after being satisfied found the under mentioned persons responsible for day to day business and as such they are in-charge of and responsible for the conduct of business.

Thus, the accused persons have violated the provisions of Section 26 (1), Section 26 (2)
(i) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 read with Section 3 (1) (zz) (v) (vii) & (viii)
of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, alongwith violation of Section 27 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

Accused also violated Regulation No.3.1.2(1) read with 3.1.2(6) of The Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additive) Regulations, 2011 which is punishable under Section 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

sentences.text:
5. Ld. Counsel for the accused has argued that the said provision i.e. Regulation 3.1.2 (1) and 3.1.2 (6) of The Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additive) Regulations,
2011 has since been amended w.e.f. 08.09.2016 and substituted and a copy of the Gazette notification has also been placed on record today.

entities.text:
Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additive) Regulations,
2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. I have perused the same.
The effect of the amendment is that the said provision 3.1.2 (1) and 3.1.2 (6) have been omitted.

Summoning order by the Ld. Magistrate is without any reasons and reads as follows:
Complaint perused.
On the basis of the complaint and other documents, prima facie, there is sufficient material to proceed against the accused persons.
Since, complainant is a public servant, his evidence U/s 200 Cr.P.C is dispensed with.
Accordingly, cognizance of the offences as mentioned in the complaint is taken.
Summons be issued to the accused persons through FSO for 29.06.2021.

7. Ld. Magistrate has not considered the effect of the amendment as well as mistake made in the complaint, if any, on this count and whether the position remains unchanged or has considerably changed pursuant to the amendment as far as use of additives is concerned.
8. I do not have the benefit of the view of the Ld. Magistrate and his interpretation to the amended provisions in the summoning order.
9. Summoning order cannot be sustained in these circumstances.
